title_en: Steady Global Economic Growth in 2027 Outlook But Risks Tilted to Downside
title_zh: 2027年全球经济展望：稳健增长但风险偏向下行
subtitle_zh: 高盛首席经济学家 Jan Hatzius 与市场策略师 Dominic Wilson 解读来年增长、通胀、利率与AI投资前景
summary_zh: 本集 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 节目中，主持人 Allison Nathan 与高盛首席经济学家 Jan Hatzius 及全球市场研究组资深顾问 Dominic Wilson 深入探讨2027年经济与市场展望。Hatzius 指出2026年全球经济增长2.7%，表现「非凡地平凡」，AI投资贡献约全球GDP的0.5个百分点。2027年基线预测为2.8%增长，但风险偏向下行，包括中东局势再度升级推高油价、多国财政不可持续引发债券收益率飙升、以及AI投资增速放缓。通胀方面，核心PCE预计从目前3%出头降至2027年底的2.4%，关税传导效应将在2027年初基本消退。货币政策方面，预计美联储12月加息25个基点，2027年初可能再加一次；欧洲央行和英国央行各加息一次；日本央行则预计加息三次至终端利率2%。Wilson 认为市场基线定价合理，股票预期正回报但幅度不及前三年；债券回报环境为2020年以来最佳；美元预计温和走软。他建议投资者注重多元化配置、能源对冲和期权保护，以应对尾部风险。就业方面，Hatzius 预计AI将在2028至2030年代初导致失业率暂时上升约0.5个百分点。
description: Steady Global Economic Growth in 2027 Outlook But Risks Tilted to Downside

turns.en: The global economy has held study this year, defying a war in the Middle East, higher tariffs, and higher interest rates. But come that resilience last. As we look forward to 2027, investors are facing a new set of questions. Will the AI boom cool down? Will higher borrowing costs hurt growth?
turns.zh: 今年全球经济保持稳定，顶住了中东战争、更高关税和更高利率的冲击。但这种韧性还能持续多久？展望2027年，投资者面临一系列新问题：AI热潮会降温吗？更高的借贷成本会损害增长吗？

turns.en: And will energy prices remain a headwind or become a tailwind? I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges.
turns.zh: 能源价格会继续构成逆风，还是会转变为顺风？我是 Allison Nathan，欢迎收听 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。

turns.en: Today we're diving into the economic and market outlook for the year ahead. I'm joined by Jan Hotsius, head of Goldman Sachs Research and the firm's chief economist and Dominic Wilson, a senior advisor in the global markets research group. Jan, don't welcome back to the program. Gradually here. Thank you.
turns.zh: 今天我们将深入探讨未来一年的经济和市场前景。我请来了 Goldman Sachs Research 主管兼公司首席经济学家 Jan Hatzius，以及全球市场研究组资深顾问 Dominic Wilson。Jan、Dom，欢迎回到节目。很高兴来到这里，谢谢。

turns.en: I can't believe another year has gone by. Another outlook report is out. Congratulations on getting it out. And there's a lot to talk about. So, Jan, as I mentioned, between the war in Iran, higher tariffs, higher rates, you would have thought the global economy would have struggled in 2026. But growth has been relatively resilient.
turns.zh: 真不敢相信又过了一年。又一份展望报告出炉了，恭喜你们完成发布。有很多话题可以聊。Jan，正如我提到的，伊朗战争、更高的关税、更高的利率——你会以为2026年全球经济会陷入困境，但增长实际上相当有韧性。

turns.en: You've actually described it this year as remarkably unremarkable in terms of growth. So, what's kept it going? 2026 has been a pretty good year, at least globally. We are on track for growth of 2.7% for the world economy that's in line with our estimate of potential. And it's not far from what we thought at the start of the year.
turns.zh: 你其实把今年的增长形容为“非凡地平凡”。那么，是什么支撑了经济增长？2026年是相当不错的一年，至少从全球来看是这样。我们预计世界经济增长2.7%，这与我们对潜在增长率的估计一致，也与我们年初的预期相差不大。

turns.en: Some of the headwinds you mentioned have been small. Tariffs, for example, were an issue in 2025, but not really in 2026. We did see an increase in interest rates, and that's taken by itself a drag on growth. But broader financial conditions have been supportive of growth for most of the year.
turns.zh: 你提到的一些逆风其实影响较小。例如关税在2025年是个问题，但在2026年并不是。我们确实看到了利率上升，这本身对增长构成拖累，但更广泛的金融条件在今年大部分时间里都支撑了增长。

turns.en: And then if you look at the war in Iran and the impact on energy prices, that's been smaller than what you would have perhaps expected given all the disruptions in the state of Hormuz. Oil prices did go up very meaningfully, but not as much as some predicted. And I certainly would have thought if you'd given me the entire chain of events
turns.zh: 再看伊朗战争对能源价格的影响，考虑到霍尔木兹海峡的所有中断，实际影响可能比你预期的要小。油价确实大幅上涨，但没有一些预测那么夸张。如果你把中东整条事件链摆在我面前，我肯定会认为影响会更大。

turns.en: in the Middle East. And I think some of that is related to pipeline redirection. Some of it is related to dark flows and escorted flows through the state. And some of it is related to reduced demand for oil, in some sense, higher price elasticity in some parts of the global economy, for example, in China.
turns.zh: 我认为部分原因与管道改道有关，部分与通过海峡的暗流和护航运输有关，还与石油需求减少有关——某种意义上，全球经济某些部分的价格弹性更高，比如中国。

turns.en: And then you had a couple of significant boosts to growth that have offset whatever drag there was. And I'd mention fiscal policy, expansionary in the US on the back of the 2025 fiscal bill in Germany on the back of the defense and infrastructure program and in Asia in terms of fuel subsidies that insulated household cash flow.
turns.zh: 此外，你还看到了几个对增长的重大提振，抵消了各种拖累。我要提到财政政策——美国在2025年财政法案推动下实行扩张性政策，德国的国防和基础设施计划，以及亚洲的燃油补贴保护了家庭现金流。

turns.en: So that's been helpful. And then lastly, of course, we've seen a big increase in AI investment throughout 2026. For the year as a whole, we think we're getting an increase that's worth about half a percent of global GDP. And that's meaningful, even though, of course, it's unequally distributed.
turns.zh: 这些都起到了帮助作用。最后，当然，我们在整个2026年看到AI投资大幅增长。就全年而言，我们认为这一增长大约相当于全球GDP的0.5个百分点。这是有意义的，尽管分配当然不均匀。

turns.en: You get a very large growth boost in East Asia, especially Taiwan and Korea. You get a moderate growth boost in the US and then something much smaller elsewhere. But for the global numbers, it's been important. But you expect some of those supports to fade in 2027 and you see risks to growth actually tilted to the downside.
turns.zh: 东亚获得非常大的增长提振，尤其是台湾和韩国。美国获得温和的增长提振，其他地区则小得多。但对全球数据来说，这很重要。不过你预计其中一些支撑因素会在2027年消退，而且你认为增长风险实际上偏向下行。

turns.en: So why the more cautious tone? The baseline is similar. We're at 2.8 percent for 2027. And yes, we're seeing the financial conditions boost fade and probably replaced by at least a moderate negative impact on growth over the next few quarters, just based on what our financial conditions indices have done.
turns.zh: 那么为什么语气更加谨慎？基线预测其实差不多，2027年为2.8%。是的，我们看到金融条件的提振正在消退，可能在未来几个季度被至少温和的负面增长影响所取代，这只是基于我们金融条件指数的走势。

turns.en: We're also probably going to get a more neutral impulse from fiscal policy. But then there are two things that are going to be helping us. One, still ongoing strong growth in AI investment. We do think that's probably going to be front-loaded. So the biggest impact in the early part of 2027,
turns.zh: 我们可能还会从财政政策获得更加中性的推动。但有两件事会帮助我们：第一，AI投资持续强劲增长。我们确实认为这可能是前置的，所以最大影响在2027年初，

turns.en: then we would expect that impact to fade as we go through the year. But for the year, as a whole, looks similar to 2026 in terms of the increase. And then we are expecting a friendlier backdrop from an energy price and energy impact on real income perspective. Our commodity strategists have oil prices gradually come down
turns.zh: 然后我们预计这一影响会随着年度推进而消退。但就全年而言，增幅看起来与2026年相似。此外，我们预计能源价格和能源对实际收入的影响将提供更加友好的背景。我们的大宗商品策略师预计油价将逐步下降，

turns.en: towards the $80 range in 2027 and that combined with the fact that we're going to be lapping the biggest increases in oil prices that should actually help household income growth increase in real terms. So that gives us the baseline. There are downside risks to the forecast. And I would say number one on oil prices,
turns.zh: 2027年降至80美元左右区间，再加上我们将度过油价最大涨幅的基数期，这实际上应该有助于家庭收入的实际增长。这就是我们的基线。预测存在下行风险。首先关于油价，

turns.en: we've seen much more positive near to our news floor before. But there is still a risk that ultimately we get an escalation, renewed escalation and renewed spike in prices that would certainly upend some of the assumptions that we've been making. We are, I think, at risk of tightening in financial conditions.
turns.zh: 我们已经看到新闻底线有了更加积极的近况，但仍然存在最终出现升级——再度升级和价格再度飙升的风险，这肯定会颠覆我们一直在做的一些假设。我认为我们面临金融条件收紧的风险，

turns.en: For example, via spikes in bond yields, fiscal policy is on an unsustainable path in a number of economies. I think that's true in the United States. I think it's true in the UK to a lesser degree. And then it's certainly true in the euro area, especially in France. We've seen significant spikes in bond yields
turns.zh: 例如通过债券收益率飙升。多个经济体的财政政策处于不可持续的轨道上，我认为美国如此，英国在较小程度上也是如此，欧元区肯定如此，尤其是法国。我们已经看到债券收益率大幅飙升，

turns.en: were working our way towards the French presidential election in April and May. And if investors don't see a clear plan for adjusting fiscal policy, then I think we're at risk of additional tensions there. And that could also spill over into broader financial conditions and slow growth. And then lastly, on AI investment,
turns.zh: 正在向4月和5月的法国总统大选推进。如果投资者没有看到调整财政政策的明确计划，我认为我们面临进一步紧张的风险。这也可能蔓延到更广泛的金融条件并拖累增长。最后，关于AI投资，

turns.en: there are a number of downside risks to this path of continued increases. Some of those are regulatory pushback against data center investment, which is something to be focused on. I don't expect a big impact, but it's a very fluid situation and obviously very politics dependent.
turns.zh: 持续增长的路径存在许多下行风险。其中一些是针对数据中心投资的监管阻力，这是需要关注的。我不预期会有重大影响，但形势非常多变，显然高度依赖政治。

turns.en: There are a lot of shortages in the semiconductor and especially memory industry, which suggests that a significant chunk of the increase in nominal spending could end up going into price rather than volume. And that would also be a downside risk for real GDP. And then there's the question of what point is the
turns.zh: 半导体尤其是存储器行业存在大量短缺，这表明名义支出增长中很大一部分可能最终流入价格而非数量。这也将成为实际GDP的下行风险。然后还有一个问题：AI资本存量的

turns.en: build out of the AI capital stock sufficiently advanced that you really see more of a slowdown in demand. In our baseline, that doesn't happen until 2028, 2029, but it's hard to time this. And so I think that's another risk to be focused on. Don, let me bring you into the conversation.
turns.zh: 建设到什么程度才算足够先进，以至于你真的会看到需求更多放缓。在我们的基线中，这要到2028、2029年才会发生，但时机很难把握。所以我认为这是另一个需要关注的风险。Dom，让我也请你加入讨论。

turns.en: We've just heard Jan's growth expectations pretty steady stable, but downside risks as he just spoke about. You know, our markets are appropriately pricing that risk. What do you make of this? Yeah, I think there's a similar balancing act going on on the market side. The baseline outlook that Jan laid out is pretty benign.
turns.zh: 我们刚刚听了 Jan 的增长预期——相当稳定，但正如他刚才谈到的存在下行风险。市场是否在适当定价这些风险？你怎么看？是的，我认为市场端也在进行类似的平衡。Jan 描述的基线前景相当温和。

turns.en: And our baseline is for positive equity returns. So risk assets to be supported by that that kind of growth picture. I don't think we're obviously underpriced to that growth view, but I do think it's a helpful tailwind if that's where we're going. I think like a lot of the last six months,
turns.zh: 我们的基线是股票正回报，风险资产得到这种增长图景的支撑。我不认为我们对这一增长观点的定价明显偏低，但我确实认为如果情况如此，这是一个有利的顺风。我认为就像过去六个月的大部分时间一样，

turns.en: that means a lot of the action in markets is going to be around these risks and the pricing of the distribution of risks. And that's where those opportunities are going to come from. And I would say, you know, there are two that are still very prominent. The oil and energy risk and the AI theme,
turns.zh: 这意味着市场中很多动作将围绕这些风险以及风险分布的定价展开，机会也将由此产生。我要说的是，有两个风险仍然非常突出：石油和能源风险，以及AI主题。

turns.en: you know, both of which, you know, I mentioned. I think that they operate on slightly different time horizons. If you look at the energy risk, as Jan said, the biggest near-term risk is probably that we get renewed escalation and a renewed energy price spike.
turns.zh: 这两者我认为在略微不同的时间范围内发挥作用。如果你看能源风险，正如 Jan 所说，最大的近期风险可能是我们再次看到局势升级和能源价格飙升。

turns.en: I think what, you know, what's happened is the market has worried a lot about that coming into the midterms, you know, our commodities team estimates the risk premium in oil markets, which is sort of how far oil is trading above where we think the fundamentals will put it. That was about $30 a few weeks ago
turns.zh: 我认为发生的情况是，进入中期选举前市场对此非常担忧。我们的大宗商品团队估计石油市场的风险溢价——也就是油价相对于我们认为基本面所支撑水平的溢价——几周前约为30美元，

turns.en: as the worries about escalation post-midterm were, you know, were particularly high. We've seen a lot of relaxation around that since that point. We're close to zero on the risk premium now. And so I would say in that sense, the market is now more vulnerable again to that near-term risk. Maybe that risk is a little underpriced.
turns.zh: 当时中期选举后对局势升级的担忧特别高。自那以后，我们看到了很多缓解。风险溢价现在接近于零。所以从这个意义上说，市场现在再次更容易受到近期风险的影响。也许这种风险有点被低估了。

turns.en: I think the biggest story, which, you know, you know, focused on is how the market handles the kind of transition in the AI story and the potential peaking of the growth impulse there. And I do think, you know, relative to the economic story, that's sort of a tougher thing for the market story.
turns.zh: 我认为最大的故事——也是市场聚焦的——是市场如何应对AI故事中的转变以及增长动力可能见顶的情况。我确实认为，相对于经济层面，这对市场来说是更棘手的问题。

turns.en: For the two reasons, the first is that, you know, the contributions that the AI investment story has made, both to CapEx, to earnings, to market value are quite a lot higher than to overall GDP growth in the US in particular. And so it's just been a bigger issue for markets than for the macro economy.
turns.zh: 原因有两个。第一，AI投资故事对资本支出、盈利和市值的贡献，远高于其对整体GDP增长的贡献，尤其是在美国。所以对市场来说，这是一个比对宏观经济更大的议题。

turns.en: And so there's this sort of more focus on those dynamics in the markets. And the second thing is that a peak in growth rates, what we think of as second derivative turning point, you know, we've found historically tends to matter more for markets. It kind of allows markets to place a limit on the upsides of distributions.
turns.zh: 因此市场对这些动态更加关注。第二点是，增长率见顶——我们所说的二阶导数转折点——历史上往往对市场更重要。它让市场能够对分布的上行空间设定上限。

turns.en: And so there tends to be more, even if growth stays strong, just the kind of slowing or the peaking of that growth rate matters. I think the market's been doing a lot of that work. So the good news is we've been derating this AI area, particularly the infrastructure producers for, you know, for a few months.
turns.zh: 所以即使增长保持强劲，仅仅是增长率的放缓或见顶也很重要。我认为市场一直在做大量这方面的工作。好消息是，几个月来我们一直在对AI领域进行估值下调，尤其是基础设施供应商。

turns.en: And so valuations are less demanding. And I think the bigger focus is now going to be on the earnings side. We've had a very sort of sharp increase in the share of earnings going as a proportion of GDP going to S&P 500 companies. That's been very supportive, but the big question is,
turns.zh: 因此估值不再那么高企。我认为更大的焦点现在将转向盈利端。我们看到了 S&P 500 公司利润占GDP比例的急剧上升，这一直非常有支撑力，但大问题是，

turns.en: how much of that is really sustainable as the investment cycle peaks and fades? You know, there are two reasons, I think, to be more optimistic about that transition. One is that, as you mentioned, the absolute rates of growth, we're going to have positive graphics growth, we're going to have positive earnings growth.
turns.zh: 当投资周期见顶并消退时，这其中有多少是真正可持续的？我认为有两个理由对这一转变更加乐观。第一，正如你提到的，增长的绝对水平——我们将有正的GDP增长、正的盈利增长。

turns.en: So even if you're slowing to some degree, that impulse is still positive and that should be helpful, that that keeps valuations in check as well. And the other thing is that there may be a kind of baton passing from the people, the infrastructure providers who have benefited a lot to some of the other parts of the economy,
turns.zh: 所以即使增速在某种程度上放缓，推动力仍然是正的，这应该有所帮助，也能控制估值。另一点是，可能会出现一种接力棒传递——从获益颇多的基础设施提供商传递到经济的其他部分，

turns.en: hyperscalers or the broader economy in terms of who is benefiting from the boom. And so our base case is that this will be a more benign version of that transition, but if you think of the risk, the risk is that some of these bigger aggregate shocks, energy, financial conditions, or just the market pulling forward that AI
turns.zh: 比如超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers）或更广泛的经济体——在谁从这波繁荣中受益的意义上。所以我们的基准情景是，这将是一个更加温和的转变版本。但如果你想到风险，风险在于一些更大的宏观冲击——能源、金融条件，或者仅仅是市场提前反映AI

turns.en: slow down that's sort of sitting further out, that those have a bigger impact. And I would say, you know, we're priced well for the baseline. Those downside risks, you know, we're still vulnerable in terms of the way the market's priced in the moment. Right. And while I asked you to focus on the downside risks,
turns.zh: 减速——那个坐在更远期的减速，这些可能产生更大影响。我要说的是，我们对基线的定价是充分的，但这些下行风险——从市场目前的定价方式来看，我们仍然容易受到冲击。好的。虽然我让你聚焦下行风险，

turns.en: you know, our mainline views are generally optimistic and steady growth. So just to be perfectly clear, your mainline expectations for asset markets is more upset. Yeah. So the mainline expectations positive for equities that is supported, the returns are less dramatic than we've seen for some of the last three years,
turns.zh: 但我们的主线观点总体上是乐观的、增长稳定的。所以为了完全明确，你对资产市场的主线预期是更加看涨的。是的。主线预期对股票是正面的，回报得到支撑，但不如过去三年中某些时期那么引人注目，

turns.en: but positive and that kind of positive baseline growth story and some of what we think on the inflation policy side are important underpinnings to that. But what I would say is if we get the risk cases, the market obviously, you know, has some vulnerability to those. We'll dig a little bit more into that in a few minutes.
turns.zh: 但是正面的。那种正面的基线增长故事以及我们在通胀政策方面的一些看法是重要支撑。但我要说的是，如果出现风险情景，市场显然对这些风险有一定脆弱性。我们几分钟后再深入探讨。

turns.en: But, John, let me turn back to you and ask about jobs always in focus. The labor market looks pretty solid. We got another relatively solid upside surprise on payrolls in the US at least recently. But AI, it does seem to be showing up a little bit more in the numbers. So talk to us about that and the risks to the job market from AI.
turns.zh: 不过 Jan，让我转回你，问问就业——始终备受关注。劳动力市场看起来相当稳固，我们最近在美国非农数据上又得到了一个相对强劲的上行惊喜。但AI似乎确实在数据中开始更加明显地体现出来。跟我们谈谈这个问题以及AI对就业市场的风险。
